messages.subject: Smote Implemention Using Rhipe
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

   I have done SMOTE Technique in R using DMwR package like below.
newData <- SMOTE(Species ~ ., data <http://inside-r.org/r-doc/utils/data>, perc.over = 600,perc.under=100).
   i want to do it in Rhipe because it communicates with Hadoop to carry out the big, parallel computations.

  Can anyone guide me how to do it in Rhipe map reduce steps.

Thanks,
Anil

messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] rhwrite(list(1,2,3),"/tmp/x") generates error "requested classic write, ..."
messages.body_plain:
My problem is that I can't get rhwrite to recognize that I am using the 'new' style.

Using the old format I can do:

> x <- list(list("a",1),list("b",2),list("c",3))

> rhwrite(x, "/tmp/x")
Wrote 0.73 KB,3 chunks, and 3 elements (100% complete)

and rhwrite will work fine, but when attempting to use the new style i still get the error even when setting the style to new:

> x <- list(1,2,3)
> rhwrite(x, "/tmp/x", style='new')
Error in rhwrite(x, "/tmp/x", style = "new") :

  You requested 'classic' write, for that one must provide a list each element of which is a list of length 2

Im using  the following packages: Rhipe_0.73.1 and datadr_0.4.1

On Thursday, August 29, 2013 10:34:16 AM UTC-5, Fishtank wrote:
> In the classi style ('old' style) the list that has to be written must of the format
>
> list( list(key,value), list(key,value),list(key,value),...,)
>
> and then you do
>
> x <- list(list("a",1),list("b",2),list("c",3))
> rhwrite(x,file="/user/sguha/tmp/x")
>
> in the new format, style='new', it is chunked by the chunk parameter (defaults to 1)
> and writes them (but in this case you dont need write a list of key,values like above)
>
> x <- list(1,2,3)
> rhwrite(x,file="/user/sguha/tmp/x2",style='new')
>
> (here default chunk is 1,rhread returns
>
>  rhread("/user/sguha/tmp/x2")[[1]]
>  [[1]]
> NULL
>
> [[2]]
> [[2]][[1]]
> [1] 1
>
> note, it returns key,values, the key is /always/ NULL (when written using 'new' style) and the value is a list (basically the shape returnedby the [] operator applied to a list)
>
>
>
>
> On Wed, Aug 28, 2013 at 11:26 AM, Joe Mihm <joe...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > Hi,
> >
> > Im pretty new to hadoop and stumbled across the Rhipe package as a great way to simplify my analysis. I started going through some of the examples, a basic rhwrite to the HDFS, and have been running into some trouble.
> >
> > > rhwrite(list(1,2,3),"/tmp/x")
> > Error in rhwrite(list(1, 2, 3), "/tmp/x") :
> >   You requested 'classic' write, for that one must provide a list each element of which is a list of length 2
> >
> >
> > and the datadr example gives the same error:
> >
> > >rhwrite(infert, file = "infertRaw", chunk = 248, style = "new")
> > Error in rhwrite(infert, file = "infertRaw", chunk = 248, style = "new") :
> >   You requested 'classic' write, for that one must provide a list each element of which is a list of length 2
> >
> > Any guidance would be appreciated. Thanks!
> >
> > Joe
> >
> > --
> >
> > ---
